transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-12
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Chen (Redwood AE); Marcus Lee (Redwood SE); Karen Morales (Northbridge - Head of Cloud Ops); Jared Thompson (Northbridge CTO); Lina Patel (Northbridge - Compliance Manager)

[00:00] Sophie: hey everyone thanks for joining on a wednesday afternoon, i'm sophie chen from redwood inference, i'll kick us off. do I have a quick round of intros?
[00:12] Karen: yeah hi i'm karen, head of cloud ops at northbridge, we run most services in AWS us-east-1 and eu-west-1.
[00:20] Jared: jared here, CTO. main thing for us is we need to understand data residency and how logs are handled for regulated workloads.
[00:28] Lina: lina, compliance. i care about auditability, retention windows, and PII handling - especially customer id and transaction details.
[00:35] Marcus: marcus from redwood, i'm the solutions engineer, i'll go deep on deployment options and what stays in your network vs what we host.
[00:44] Sophie: great. quick agenda: 1) understand current stack & constraints 2) compliance requirements (gdpr, relevant finserv regs) 3) discuss hosted vs dedicated vs private options 4) next steps. sound good?
[00:52] Karen: yes.

[02:05] Sophie: to start, karen you mentioned aws regions. what is your requirement for eu data residency - do you need all eu traffic and storage to stay in eu, or just eu customer data?
[02:18] Karen: primarily EU customer data needs to be resident in eu. for some services we can do regional routing, but the default is we cannot send raw customer data outside eu borders.
[02:29] Marcus: ok so that's a common pattern. redwood hosted offers region selection for endpoints, we have hosting in eu-west-1, but the trick is logs and some metadata - are you comfortable with those flowing to our control plane in the us?
[02:45] Karen: no - they need to be either encrypted and non-reversible, or better they should not leave our vpc.
[02:53] Sophie: that's where dedicated and private come in. dedicated gives reserved capacity in a region and can be configured to keep customer data isolated, but the control plane may still be managed. private gives you a customer-managed control plane or an on-prem bundle.
[03:10] Jared: can you explain the difference in terms of audit logs and access? like who has access to raw request logs?
[03:18] Marcus: sure, so by default hosted logs are stored in redwood's logs with role-based access - we do SOC2 controls - but that means logs traverse our control plane. with dedicated, logs can be segmented per-tenant and we can restrict human access; with private we can keep logs entirely in your network, with optional S3-compatible sinks under your account and a KMS key you control.
[03:39] Lina: when you say KMS key we mean our aws-kms key? or do you support HSM?
[03:45] Marcus: we support customer-managed KMS in aws and also integrations with HSMs for private deployments - it's called KMS/HSM integration. for hosted we manage keys but can do envelope encryption and purge key material on request.
[03:59] Karen: okay that's helpful. second, for gdpr we may need to show data flows and ensure we can delete personal data upon request. is there a supported delete API for user data?
[04:12] Sophie: yes, we have delete and retention controls. in private you get full control. in dedicated we can provide deletion workflows and also limited retention windows. in hosted we provide retention controls and redact/pseudonymize options but it's more bounded.

[05:30] Jared: what's the timeline for private deployment? if we need a private control plane in our vpc how long does that take?
[05:38] Marcus: typical onboarding for private is 6-8 weeks including security review; dedicated is faster - 2-4 weeks - because it's our managed infra but in your dedicated tenancy. hosted is immediate.
[05:49] Sophie: also worth noting cost delta: private has higher baseline fees for the package and support, dedicated is in between, hosted is pay-as-you-go. we'll send a ballpark cost model.

[07:02] Lina: log retention: regulators want 7 years for some transaction logs. can redwood guarantee retention and provide immutable audit trails?
[07:12] Marcus: yes, for private we can store logs in your s3 with immutability and object lock if you need WORM. for dedicated we can provide retention policies and export to your storage account. hosted can keep for configurable windows but longest retention is usually an add-on.
[07:30] Karen: what about masking - can we redact PII before logs leave our network?
[07:36] Marcus: we have prefix masking and prompt-level PII redaction built into the runtime; in private you can run a pre-send hook to fully strip or tokenize PII before it's sent to the model.

[09:00] Sophie: are there any certifications you require - SOC 2, ISO, or others?
[09:07] Lina: yes SOC2 attestation is table stakes, and we'll ask for evidence during vendor onboarding. we may also need penetration test reports and vendor security questionnaires.
[09:18] Marcus: we can provide SOC2 Type II reports, ISO-27001 summary, and also can work with your security team for pen tests. we'll include those artifacts.

[10:40] Karen: question on model variants: if we run in private, can we still use the same model catalog and updates from redwood? or do we get a frozen model?
[10:50] Marcus: you can opt-in to model updates; in private we support model mirroring where we pull vetted model artifacts into your environment; for strict change control we can pin versions. the runtime supports quantized variants too.

[13:05] Jared: network - does private require peering or a VPN? and how do we manage egress?
[13:13] Marcus: private typically uses VPC peering or AWS Transit Gateway and an EKS/private subnet install. all egress can be controlled by your routing rules and NAT; for secrets you can integrate with your KMS/HSM. we provide terraform modules to simplify setup.

[15:40] Lina: regulatory nuance - for some EU customers we need a Data Processing Addendum and SCCs. does redwood sign DPS/DPAs and enter SCCs for hosted customers?
[15:52] Sophie: yes we have standard DPA and SCCs for EU controls; for private we adapt contract terms as needed. we'll share our legal templates.

[18:00] Karen: one of our blockers is the requirement that logs containing transaction identifiers not be searchable by vendor staff. can you support encryption-at-rest where only northbridge holds the decryption key?
[18:14] Marcus: yes, that's customer-managed key (CMK) model. you control the KMS key. Redwood would not be able to decrypt without key access. we also support split-keystore models if you need multi-party control.

[20:10] Sophie: any concerns about latency? jordan - sorry jared - do you have SLOs?
[20:18] Jared: we target sub-200ms for short prompts and low hundreds for longer chat flows in product-critical paths. can dedicated meet that?
[20:25] Marcus: dedicated in-region is designed for low latency; for hot paths we recommend a dedicated pool pinned to the application with KV caching. we typically hit sub-100ms for small requests on A100-class instances; private performance depends on your hardware. we'll run a benchmark.

[23:00] Karen: budget question: can you share an example pricing for dedicated vs private for a medium bank?
[23:10] Sophie: we'll put together a cost model - but expect private to have an upfront platform/license and higher support tier; dedicated is more predictable monthly reserved capacity; hosted is variable. we'll send examples.

[26:30] Lina: on HIPAA - not core for us but some flows with healthcare data in an insurance vertical need HIPAA safeguards. do you have BAAs?
[26:38] Marcus: we can sign a BAA for private and dedicated workflows; hosted may be limited depending on deployment and controls. we'll circle back with legal.

[29:00] Jared: curious about rollback and model audit - if a model update degrades quality, can we control rollouts?
[29:09] Marcus: yes rollout controls, canary deploys, pin versions, automatic fallback to previous variant. we also have eval tooling to detect regression against your test prompts.

[31:20] Karen: what does the redwood control plane see from our traffic? are prompts stored in plain text?
[31:28] Marcus: in hosted prompts are logged for observability and debugging but we provide redaction and retention policies. for dedicated we can disable prompt logging or only store hashed digests; for private, logs never leave your env unless you configure exports.

[34:00] Lina: we also need to know who within redwood has elevated access - request a list of roles that could access production logs and whether it's audited.
[34:10] Sophie: we'll provide a people/roles access matrix and recent audit logs as part of the security package.

[36:45] Karen: ok feels like private is the safest from a compliance stance but it's longer to provision. do you have customers in finserv running private?
[36:54] Marcus: yes, we have a few bank customers running private/on-prem bundles and several running dedicated with strict controls. we'll anonymize case studies in the pack.

[38:10] Sophie: recap and next steps - action items we captured: sophie will send SOC2, iso, dpa and legal templates plus KMS notes; marcus will set up a perf benchmark and provide a dedicated vs private cost sketch; lina will provide northbridge compliance checklist and required audit fields; then we'll schedule a follow up call with infra and legal to finalize scope.
[38:35] Jared: sounds good.
[38:40] Lina: thanks, please include pen test and vulnerability disclosure details.
[38:46] Marcus: will do.
[40:00] Sophie: any final q's?
[40:05] Karen: no, thanks everyone.
[40:10] Sophie: thanks all, i'll send notes and the artifact links. bye.

Meeting artifacts mentioned: security whitepaper, SOC2 report, DPA/SCC templates, KMS integration notes, perf benchmark spreadsheet (links to be shared).

End of transcript.
